title: 1971 AHSME Problem 17
statement: A circular disk is divided by \(2n\) equally spaced radii \((n\gt0)\) and one secant line. The maximum number of nonoverlapping areas into which the disk can be divided is:

solutions.text:
The radii first make \(2n\) sectors. A secant not through the center can meet at most one radius in each of \(n\) opposite pairs, hence at most \(n\) radii. Those intersections divide the secant chord into \(n+1\) pieces, each of which adds one region. The maximum is therefore \(2n+(n+1)=3n+1.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Begin with the \(2n\) sectors made by the radii
A secant can cross at most \(n\) of the radii, so count the pieces of the secant chord
